doc: THE 4TH-NEAREST LUMP AND THE DOME PEAK. On this draw the dome at texels (row 23, col 6) and (row 60, col 25) comes from the FOURTH-nearest lump (a lower radius loses to a farther, wider one): a max over the 3 nearest would be lower there by 5.6e-04 and 2.0e-02. The texel (row 16, col 37) lies at dist / r = 0.0012 of a lump center, where the dome is 0.99925: the upper bound of clip(1 - dist / r, 0, 1) never binds (dist >= 0), so the dome rises to 1 at a center with no flat top; a port that caps it below 1, say at 0.99, loses 6e-3 here. Both facts are invisible on a typical draw (lumps.s64), hence the searched seed. The jittered lump grid (60 x 60 = 3600 centers g, [x, y] in tile units, and their radii r (0.35 to 0.7 of the spacing)) is the input (plan0.g, plan0.r); freq = round(240 / 4) = 60 is read from the source (params.constants). dome = max over the 4 NEAREST lumps (by distance, periodic KD tree, not by normalized distance) of clip(1 - dist / r, 0, 1)^0.6. Measured: every random input nudged by one float64 ulp (8 trials) and numpy.fft replaced by scipy.fft: max |diff| 6e-14, because x^0.6 has an infinite slope at 0 (a distance within an ulp of r moves the value by up to (1e-16)^0.6 = 1.6e-10): 1e-9 relative, 1e-9 absolute.
